name: BSc Environmental Science
title: BSc Environmental Science
intro: The environmental science roadmap: admission, ecology and environmental chemistry papers, fieldwork and careers in consulting and government.
glance: MSc Env. Sci., EIA, pollution control

phases.title: Class 11–12 subjects
phases.summary: Science with Biology or Maths alongside Physics and Chemistry.
points: Most universities accept Class 12 Science (PCB or PCM); some accept any stream with Biology or Geography.
Build basics in Biology, Chemistry and Geography.
Observe local environmental problems such as waste, water and air pollution.
Read about climate change, biodiversity and environmental law.

phases.title: Entrance exams and admission
phases.summary: CUET-UG for central universities, merit or entrance for others.
points: Take CUET-UG with the required science domain subjects.
Apply through university counselling portals.
State and private universities admit through merit lists or tests.
Prefer colleges with field stations, labs and EIA project exposure.

phases.title: Year 1: foundation papers
phases.summary: Core science papers and lab skills.
points: Core papers: Ecology and Ecosystems, Environmental Chemistry, Geology and Soil Science, and Environmental Studies.
Under NEP you also take language, environment and skill-enhancement courses.
Learn to maintain a lab notebook, follow safety rules and write practical reports.
Start reading beyond the syllabus and attend department seminars.

phases.title: Year 2–3: advanced and applied papers
phases.summary: Deeper papers, electives and a project.
points: Year 2: Environmental Microbiology, Pollution (Air, Water and Soil), Climate Science, and Statistics for Environmental Data.
Year 3: Environmental Impact Assessment, Environmental Law and Policy, Waste Management, GIS and Remote Sensing, and a field-based dissertation.
Complete a project or dissertation under a faculty guide.
Many universities offer a fourth Honours year with research.

phases.title: Lab skills, internships and training
points: Learn: water, air and soil testing, ecological surveys, GIS (QGIS/ArcGIS), data analysis and EIA report writing.
Do summer internships or short research projects in labs, companies and government institutions.
Take certificate courses on SWAYAM, NPTEL or industry bodies.
Keep a record of your projects, certificates and skills.

phases.title: After BSc: MSc, exams and careers
phases.summary: Master’s degree, NET/JRF, government jobs or industry.
points: Further study and careers: MSc Environmental Science, EIA and ESG consulting, waste management, pollution control boards, forestry, NGO and CSR roles.
Exams: CUET-PG, CSIR-UGC NET, state pollution control board recruitment, UPSC (Indian Forest Service) and state PSCs.
Research route: MSc, then CSIR-UGC NET (JRF) or GATE and a PhD.
Government exams such as SSC and state PSCs are open to science graduates.
facts: CUET-PG, CSIR-UGC NET, state pollution control board recruitment, UPSC (Indian Forest Service) and state PSCs
